mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility has risen consistently from -2.0% to +2.3% over four weeks, signaling restored confidence in essential errands. This confidence diffuses to discretionary retail within the same shopping trip, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 4.3 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above +1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility has stabilized at -28% for two consecutive weeks, indicating commuting patterns have reached a floor. When transit stabilizes, workers shift to alternative mobility modes and retail-adjacent activities, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change falls below 1 percentage point for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 14 days when TRANSIT stabilization is observed, or TRANSIT resumes sharp decline.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has improved from -14.9% to -12.6% over four weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated at 14.6%. This combination indicates outdoor recreation is substituting for indoor retail. If parks continue improving and residential remains high, RETAIL_REC will decline as outdoor activities capture discretionary time.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10% AND RESIDENTIAL remains above 14%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 2.3 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite parks improving and residential remaining elevated, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 13%.

Persistent workplace suppression indicates ongoing restrictions or voluntary avoidance. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as foot traffic sources remain constrained.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains between -16% and -18% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES range -17.1% to -15.6% with no upward trend
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES remains in the -16% to -18% band, or WORKPLACES rises above -14%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved 1.3 percentage points over four weeks (-19.0% to -17.7%), establishing a consistent upward micro-trend. This trend is independent of external shocks and reflects seasonal or calendar-driven recovery. The trend will continue over the next four weeks, producing further RETAIL_REC gains.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 1.3 points over four weeks with positive slope every week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next 28 days, or the week-on-week improvement reverses to negative.

This inverse relationship indicates people are leaving homes for activities. If residential continues declining and TRANSIT remains stable, RETAIL_REC will rise as people redirect outdoor time toward retail venues.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 0.7 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 14 days when residential falls and transit stabilizes, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 15%.

Consumers will substitute indoor retail for outdoor activities, driving RETAIL_REC upward over one week.

Under this dual suppression, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed because the primary foot-traffic generators (commuters and office workers) are absent. RETAIL_REC will decline or stagnate over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite both transit and workplace mobility remaining suppressed, or either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises above -10%.
